home-equity-loan-calculator.assumptionNote: Lenders typically let you borrow up to 80% of the home's value minus the mortgage balance; the payment is capped at that maximum and assumes a fixed rate.
benefits: Find out exactly how much equity you can borrow against before calling a bank.
See the real monthly payment for any loan amount and term.
The LTV check warns you before you request more than lenders allow.
Free, instant, and private - no bank appointment needed.

faqs.a: Equity is the part of your home you truly own: home value minus mortgage balance. On a $400,000 home with a $280,000 mortgage, your equity is $120,000.
Most lenders cap total borrowing at 80-85% of the home's value. So max loan = 80% x home value - mortgage balance. On a $400,000 home with a $280,000 mortgage, the maximum is $40,000.
faqs.q: How much can I borrow against my equity?

faqs.a: A home equity loan gives one lump sum at a fixed rate and term - predictable payments. A HELOC is a revolving credit line with a variable rate. Pick the loan for a fixed project cost, the HELOC for ongoing or uncertain needs.
faqs.q: Home equity loan vs HELOC - which is better?

faqs.a: The same amortization formula as any loan: payment = loan x r / (1 - (1+r)^-n). Borrowing $40,000 at 8% for 15 years gives $382.30 per month.
faqs.q: How is the monthly payment calculated?

faqs.a: It can be lower than credit cards or personal loans because the loan is secured by your home. But it is still debt against your house - and rates are higher than first-mortgage rates.
faqs.q: Is the rate lower than a personal loan?

faqs.a: Yes. Your home is the collateral, so missed payments can lead to foreclosure. This is often called a second mortgage for a reason: treat it with the same seriousness as your first.
faqs.q: Can I lose my home with a home equity loan?

home-equity-loan-calculator.formula:
Equity = home value - mortgage balance
Max loan = 80% x home value - mortgage balance (lender cap)
Monthly payment = loan x r / (1 - (1+r)^-n), with r = annual rate/12, n = years x 12
LTV after = (mortgage balance + loan) / home value x 100
howTo: Enter what you still owe on the mortgage.
Enter the loan amount you want.
Enter the rate and term in years.
Read the payment, your equity, the maximum loan, and the resulting LTV.
keyFacts: Home equity = home value minus mortgage balance.
Lenders usually cap borrowing at 80% of value minus the mortgage.
A home equity loan is a fixed lump sum with a fixed rate and term.
It is a second mortgage: your home is the collateral.
Longer terms lower the payment but raise total interest.
